description: Solo software engineering student who is driven to make scientific knowledge and data more accessible, understandable, and useful for a better future.
summary:
Geleceğin Tarımı is a bilingual (Turkish/English) web app that helps farmers in Türkiye adapt their crop rotations to a changing climate. A farmer draws their field on a satellite map, enters their current crops, water supply and priorities, and gets their current rotation compared with two alternatives. Each option is scored on water, climate, soil, erosion, pests and income, and shows its tradeoffs, risks and a confidence level.

The decisions rest on NASA data: 20 years of NASA POWER climate for all 81 provinces (frost, heat, dry years, crop water use), GRACE/GRACE-FO groundwater trends, SRTM slope, HWSD soil, MODIS NDVI, and live SMAP and VIIRS satellite maps. Official Turkish sowing calendars and TÜİK statistics keep results grounded in real farming. A 7-day alert view and a “Would this crop work here?” check turn the data into daily decisions.

An auditable rule engine makes every decision, and every result names its source. AI only rewords the results in plain language, and any number it adds that isn’t in the data is rejected. As droughts and heat increase, farmers need advice they can trust and check, not a black box.
details:
What it does and how it works

Geleceğin Tarımı is a decision-support web app for farmers in all 81 provinces of Türkiye, in Turkish and English. A farmer marks their field on a satellite map (or picks a province) and enters their current rotation, rain-fed or irrigated water, soil type and priorities: saving water, soil health, income or simplicity. The app then offers six views:

  • Overview: hot days, yearly rain, the groundwater trend, the best rotation for their priorities, and a “driest window” chart with a plain-language explanation of what it means for their own crops.
  • Compare rotations: the farmer’s current rotation next to two alternatives, each scored 0-100 on water, climate, soil, erosion, pests, income and simplicity, with evidence, risks, information gaps, a confidence level, and how the score holds up at +2 °C and with 10% less rain.
  • Crop check: “Would this crop work here?” gives a verdict with reasons, how much irrigation water the crop needs (mm, m³ per dekar and per hectare), and better alternatives.
  • Today: a 7-day forecast checked against the limits of the crop in the field, with frost, heat, heavy-rain and dry-week alerts and good spraying hours.
  • Climate & trends: 20 years of local climate history, a measured 2020-24 vs 2005-19 climate shift with a test for noise, and a live NASA satellite map.
  • My field: up to four field parts, each with its own crops, water and soil.

A rule engine makes all decisions. Hard filters remove crops that can’t work on the field (frost, heat at flowering, too little warmth or water). Seven scores are weighted by the farmer’s priorities, published rotation rules adjust them, and an FAO-56 water balance estimates crop water use.

NASA data used

  • NASA POWER: 20 years of daily climate for every province, plus a live feed for drawn fields.
  • GRACE/GRACE-FO: groundwater and land water-storage trends.
  • SRTM: field slope.
  • HWSD (ORNL DAAC): topsoil texture.
  • MODIS NDVI: greenness through the year.
  • NASA GIBS: live VIIRS vegetation, SMAP soil moisture and land-temperature maps.

These are combined with Türkiye’s official TAGEM-DSİ sowing calendars (29 climate zones), TÜİK province crop statistics and FAO crop parameters.

Benefits

  • Tradeoffs, not one answer. Farmers see what each option gains and risks.
  • Transparent. Every result names its source, says whether it’s a NASA observation, a model or official statistics, and lists what the app doesn’t know.
  • Farmer-friendly units. Water amounts come in m³ per dekar, and alerts say what to do but never give fertilizer or pesticide doses.
  • Works without a connection. All 81 provinces’ climate data is bundled with the app; only the forecast, AI summary and drawn-field details need the internet.

Intended impact

Turkish agriculture faces more heat, drier summers and falling groundwater. GRACE data shows Çukurova (Adana) losing about 2 cm of stored water a year. The app helps farmers pick rotations that use less water and protect the soil, prepare for frost and heat before they happen, and see how their local climate is actually changing, in their own language. It supports the farmer’s judgment and always suggests checking with a local agronomist.

Tools and technologies

  • App: React 18, Vite 6, JavaScript (ES modules), Leaflet for maps, Chart.js.
  • Data preparation: Node.js and Python (netCDF4, numpy, xlrd) scripts that reduce about 34 MB of raw NASA data to a 1.6 MB bundle.
  • AI wording: Google Gemini and Anthropic Claude.
  • Server and hosting: serverless functions on Vercel.
  • Other services: Open-Meteo forecasts, Esri satellite imagery.
  • Testing: 110 automated tests with Node’s test runner, plus a data-consistency checker.
  • Hardware: standard laptops.
  • Development: AI coding assistants were used for writing and reviewing code and documentation.

What makes it creative

  • AI writes, it never decides. The rules make every decision. AI only rewords the result, and any number in its text that isn’t in the data is rejected, so it can’t invent a yield, date or risk.
  • Observed farming overrules the model. Where TÜİK statistics show farmers already growing a crop on at least 1,000 ha in a province, a failed model check becomes a warning instead of a removal.
  • Limits checked against reality. A 35 °C heat limit wrongly flagged Edirne, Türkiye’s top rice province, in 18 of 20 years, so we moved to FAO AquaCrop’s 40 °C value. We also found a dataset scaling factor that hid Adana’s groundwater decline and corrected it.
  • Explanations tied to the farmer’s own crops. For example: “So this means: your wheat flowers in May, inside the dry stretch.”

Factors the team considered

  • Trust: every number traceable to a source, honest confidence levels, and crop values marked unverified until an agronomist checks them.
  • Safety: no fertilizer or spray doses, and climate scenarios re-rank options but never silently delete them.
  • Data resolution: POWER cells are tens of kilometres wide, and the app says so.
  • Privacy: the AI never sees coordinates, place names or farmer details, and choices are saved only in the farmer’s own browser.
  • Access: Turkish crop names, dekar and dönüm units, phone-friendly layout, and offline use.
  • Free-tier limits: pre-written AI texts and saved answers keep requests low.
